To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
NDV RNA, not the virion, was the IFN-inducing component of NDV and that NDV IFN induction was a primary event.
(i) NDV mutants that are temperature-sensitive for IFN induction have been isolated; (ii) NDV mutants have been isolated that are temperature-sensitive with respect to the induction of IFN, but

1) NDV RNA synthesis and IFN induction were affected by the temperature-sensitive mutation of NDV, and 2) NDV RNA immediately synthesized after infection (primary NDV RNA synthesis) plays a key part in the IFN induction process
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the molecular mechanisms of IFN induction by NDV.
the study of the mechanisms by which NDV induces IFN, and the results obtained so far indicate the importance of the early steps of the virus life cycle in the IFN-inducing process.
the study of interferon production by viruses and the mechanism by which they induce interferon.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
IFN is induced by the primary transcription products of the virus.
IFN induction is a complex process involving several viral genes, and that the primary transcript is a key element for the induction.
the primary transcription of NDV RNA plays an important role in IFN inducibilty, and that NDV IFN induction is a complex process which is not yet fully understood.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

IFN induction by NDV is not a function of the viral genome, but rather is dependent on the appearance of a particular RNA species, which may be the result of a specific interaction between viral and host cell factors.
the NDV genome has at least 2 regions involved in IFN induction, one of them being the region coding for the viral RNA polymerase.
NDV IFN induction in primary CE cells is a multigenic function and that the primary transcription of NDV is the key step for this function.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we have identified a temperature sensitive mutant of Newcastle disease virus that can be used as a vaccine vector.
we have identified two NDV temperature-sensitive mutants that affect interferon induction.
the appearance of viral RNA immediately after infection is a key factor in IFN induction.
